subject: Inference capacity evaluation: next-priority tests & mutual action plan
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Price <jonathan.price@acmeai.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-25T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed next-priority tests

Hi Jonathan —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of next-priority tests so we can baseline cost/latency tradeoffs versus your hyperscaler runs: 

Summary notes from discovery:
- Primary workload: multi-turn customer support summarization + retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
- Peak concurrency expected: ~120 qps across 8k active users; typical seq lengths ~1k tokens for end-to-end; 95th percentile length ~1.8k.
- Data residency: US-only for PII workloads; some redacted telemetry to S3.
- Procurement: moving toward an annual reserved-capacity commitment if performance/cost delta is favorable.

Proposed immediate tests (goal: 2-week quick bench + one production soak):
1) Baseline latency & unit-cost: run your standard RAG pipeline on our Hosted API with a Dedicated pool sized to match the equivalent hyperscaler reserved GPU (16x A100-equivalent). Focus on median and P95 token latencies and per-token cost.
2) Peak concurrency stress: synthetic fanout to 150 qps sustained for 20 minutes to observe autoscaling/burst behavior and tail latency.
3) Cold-cache vs warm-cache: measure first-token latency (cold KV cache) and after 10k prefix tokens.
4) Fallback behavior: configure automatic fallback to a quantized variant for token budgets and validate output quality on a ~100-case prompt set.

Deliverables we will provide: a bench report (CSV + charts), a short ops playbook for your SREs, and a suggested Mutual Action (MA) plan if results meet your thresholds. I attached a short brief that contrasts Dedicated commitments vs typical hyperscaler reserved capacity and an initial MA spreadsheet.

As for next steps: can you confirm the target performance thresholds for P95 end-to-end (tokens) and the procurement timeline your team is aiming for? If those look good I’ll schedule the bench window and loop in our infra team.

Best,
Monica
Monica Patel | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0173

Attachment: RDW-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler-brief.pdf (summary brief)
From: Jonathan Price <jonathan.price@acmeai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed next-priority tests

Hi Monica —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 
- For procurement, our target is to make a decision by end of January. We can commit to a 12‑18 month reserved purchase if the P95 tail latency and failure modes meet our SLOs.
- Target SLOs: P95 end-to-end (token-based) <= 320 ms for single-shot prompts; for multi-turn RAG flows we’re flexible up to ~600 ms P95 if cost reductions are meaningful.
- Our infra team prefers tests run during PST business hours and we can provide a small representative dataset (~1.2GB of embeddings) and a 100-prompt QA set for quality checks.

We’re good to proceed with the three test buckets you outlined. Please include a short section in the MA plan that codifies rollback/fallback criteria (e.g., when to route to a cheaper quantized model vs keep running on higher-tier model).

Thanks — I’ll loop in procurement (procure@acmeai.com) separately.

— Jonathan
Jonathan Price | VP of Product, Acme AI
jonathan.price@acmeai.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-27T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap + proposed next-priority tests

Team — forwarding the prospect reply. Jonathan confirmed SLOs and procurement timeline. Need engineering input for the bench window and recommended Dedicated pool sizing. Highlights and asks: 

Highlights:
- Target decision: end of Jan.
- P95 targets: <=320ms for single-shot, <=600ms for RAG flows.
- Dataset: 1.2GB embeddings + 100 QA prompts.

Asks:
1) What Dedicated pool config will map closest to their hyperscaler reserved 16x A100-equivalent? If possible, provide an ops-level config and anticipated steady-state token cost.
2) Can we run a controlled stress test during PST business hours next week (preferred windows: 11/30 09:00-12:00 or 12/01 13:00-16:00 PST)?
3) Sean: can you draft rollback/fallback criteria text for the MA plan (we’ll include quantized fallback thresholds and safety margins).

I attached the MA spreadsheet draft and the competitive brief I sent Jonathan. Please reply with short bullets — don’t need a long doc.

Thanks,
Monica

Attachment: ma-plan-acmeai-20261130.xlsx
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-27T14:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + proposed next-priority tests

Monica —

Quick bullets based on infra capacity + SLO mapping: 
1) Pool sizing: recommend a Dedicated pool with 8x H100v2 (or equivalent) nodes fronted by a small burstable pool (2 nodes) to handle short spikes. H100v2 gives better throughput for KV cache heavy RAG when properly sharded; cost estimates attached in the brief.
2) Expected steady-state: based on their token distribution, estimated unit token cost on Redwood Dedicated should be ~18–22% lower than the hyperscaler reserved SKU when amortized across a 12‑month commit (this assumes our batching and prefix caching configs are enabled).
3) Bench windows: 11/30 09:00-11:30 PST is ideal. We’ll run three passes: cold-cache latency, warm-cache throughput climb to 150 qps, quality check on the 100-prompt set.
4) Rollback/fallback (MA language for procurement):
   - If P95 tail latency exceeds 500ms on two consecutive bench passes OR error rate >1% sustained over 5 minutes, automatically route 30% of traffic to the quantized variant and notify SRE.
   - If after routing to quantized variant user-perceived quality drop (measured by the 100-case prompt set) exceeds 6% failure delta vs baseline, trigger escalation to run additional capacity or switch to hyperscaler fallback per agreement.

I’ll be available to run the bench on 11/30 morning. Rishi, please confirm we have the test image and the quantized variant ready.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher | Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

- Dataset upload location (S3 link) provided?

If you’re good I’ll send a calendar invite with the runbook and the temporary test credentials. We’ll publish the bench report within 48 hours and include cost modeling to compare Dedicated vs the hyperscaler reserved SKU for your expected utilization patterns.

Best,
